name: De La Soul
sources: style-research-extended vol.1 boom-bap — De La Soul
notes: "Keys unpredictable" is authored literally: fourteen key centres at near-equal weight and six scales, which is the widest tonal spread in this batch and the only place a lydian or major-pentatonic loop can turn up. The second signature the research names by name is "frenetic" hats — `base` pinned to 16ths and `fillDensity` 0.72, the highest here — and the third is the 808 conga and hand-percussion palette, four perc lanes at [2,4] per bar. Because the loop is several unrelated sources stacked, `chordToneBias` drops to 0.55, `halfStepDissonance` rises to 0.2 and `dissonanceBudget` carries an m2 of 0.25: the bitonal clashes the research describes are a stacking artefact, so they belong in the dissonance budget rather than in a chord family. ⛔ `impliedByRiff` is set, because the research's harmony is "I–IV major vamps and modal drones" — that is a texture, not a progression — with `chordDurationBeats` 2–16 and a 39-semitone voicing register carrying the variety. ⚠ The I–bVII family at weight 2 is INFERRED: it is the mixolydian drone a library or folk record implies, and the research names no such chord. ⚠ The countermelody is "often a second sample rather than an instrument", so `fillGapsOnly` is false and `densityRatio` is 0.6 — it is allowed to collide with the lead, which is the point. ⚠ `medium` because the research rates it high-medium; the gear and method are first-person, the tempo band is catalogue-level. ⚠ An authored `chords.dissonanceBudget` was removed: no generator reads it, so it was a knob that looked like a parameter and did nothing. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 46 to 44 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 45 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 2. ⚠ `countermelody.fillGapsOnly` returned to true. With it off and a density of 0.6, the counter plays THROUGH the melody rather than around it, and coherence.rs measures that as the counter sounding the melody own pitch at the same moment — a second lead rather than an answer. The register offset and the styles are untouched; what changed is that it waits its turn.
